learn.title: Offshore Wind Farms: Design & Grid Connection
learn.intro: Offshore wind farms harness stronger, more consistent winds than onshore installations, offering vast renewable potential. IRENA highlights their role in decarbonizing energy systems, while addressing technical challenges in design, installation, and grid integration to ensure reliable power delivery.
learn.c1_text: Offshore turbines are larger (15+ MW capacity) with robust foundations like monopiles or floating platforms. Like city planning, spacing turbines 10x rotor diameter maximizes efficiency. IRENA notes these farms can generate 50% more energy than onshore equivalents in optimal locations.
learn.c2_text: Installation requires specialized vessels and seabed preparation. Water depths up to 3,000m demand floating turbines. IRENA reports 70% of global offshore wind is in waters <60m, reducing costs. Projects like Hornsea 2 (1.4 GW) showcase engineering precision.
learn.c3_text: High-voltage direct current (HVDC) cables transmit power efficiently over long distances. India’s 60 GW offshore target by 2030 requires HVDC infrastructure. IRENA states HVDC reduces losses by 30% compared to AC, enabling stable grid integration.
learn.stat2: India's offshore wind target: 60 GW by 2030

learn.title: Rooftop Solar: Net Metering & Functionality
learn.intro: Rooftop solar transforms buildings into power generators, supported by India’s net metering policies. MNRE emphasizes its role in decentralizing energy, reducing grid strain, and empowering households and businesses to manage electricity costs sustainably.
learn.c1_text: Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight into DC electricity, inverted to AC for home use. Like a water wheel harnessing flow, panels generate 4-5 kWh/m²/day in India. MNRE notes India ranks 5th globally in rooftop solar potential (600 GW).
learn.c2_text: Excess power is fed back to the grid, earning credits via bidirectional meters. MNRE’s 2016 policy allows 1:1 tariff exchange. A 1 kW system can save ₹80,000 annually. Net metering reduces peak demand, easing grid stress.
learn.c3_text: MNRE’s Rooftop Solar Programme targets 40 GW by 2022, with subsidies for residential users. States like Gujarat offer 30% capital subsidies. Over 6.8 GW installed as of 2023, demonstrating policy impact on adoption rates.

learn.title: Pumped Hydro Storage: World's Largest Battery
learn.intro: Pumped hydro storage (PHS) provides grid-scale energy storage by pumping water uphill during low demand and releasing it to generate power when needed. IRENA cites PHS as critical for balancing renewables, storing 90% of global grid storage capacity.
learn.c1_text: Two reservoirs at different elevations are connected by pipes. During surplus energy, water is pumped uphill (storing potential energy). When needed, water flows down through turbines, generating electricity. Like a gravity-powered battery, efficiency is 70-85%.
learn.c2_text: PHS accounts for 94% of global energy storage capacity (227 GW). IRENA notes it provides 16-hour storage at 20-30% cost of batteries. China’s 2.3 GW Zhangbei project exemplifies large-scale deployment for grid stability.
learn.c3_text: India’s 3,150 MW PHS capacity includes the 1,000 MW Nathpa Jhakri plant (first of its kind). MNRE highlights PHS as key to integrating 500 GW renewables by 2030. Projects like Chandaria (1,000 MW) will enhance regional grid resilience.

learn.title: Vehicle-to-Grid Tech: EVs Stabilize Grid
learn.intro: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology enables electric vehicles to supply power back to the grid, enhancing stability and renewable integration. IRENA highlights V2G as a game-changer for smart mobility, turning EVs into mobile energy resources.
learn.c1_text: V2G uses bidirectional inverters to transfer power from EV batteries to the grid. Like a two-way street, it allows charging during low demand and discharging during peaks. IRENA notes 100 kWh EV batteries can power 10 homes for a day.
learn.c2_text: Aggregated EV fleets provide frequency regulation and peak shaving. IRENA estimates V2G can reduce grid costs by 20-30% in urban areas. California’s Clean Energy Transportation Initiative pilots this for renewable integration.
learn.c3_text: India’s FAME II scheme incentivizes V2G-ready EVs. Tata Motors’ Ultraviolette P7X prototype demonstrates 7.5 kW V2G capability. With 7,000 EV charging stations, India aims for 30% EV adoption by 2030, leveraging V2G for grid support.
learn.stat3: Tata Motors’ V2G prototype: 7.5 kW output

learn.title: ISTS Waiver Policy: Cutting Interstate Renewable Costs
learn.intro: India’s ISTS waiver policy reduces interstate transmission costs for renewable projects, accelerating deployment. MNRE cites this as pivotal for achieving 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, removing barriers to rural and desert solar/wind projects.
learn.c1_text: ISTS mandates transmission access but imposed high charges for interstate renewable evacuation. Waivers exempt projects in green energy corridors from 100% ISTS charges. MNRE notes waivers saved ₹15,000 crore in transmission costs for 25 GW projects.
learn.c2_text: Waivers lowered LCOE by 15-20% for renewable developers. ISTS reforms in 2022 allowed state utilities to bear 50% of transmission costs. Projects in Rajasthan and Gujarat saw tariffs drop to ₹2.50/kWh vs ₹4.50/kWh pre-waiver.
learn.c3_text: Waiver policy enabled 25 GW renewable capacity addition in 2022-23. MNRE reports solar tariffs fell to record lows (₹2.44/kWh in 2023). States like Tamil Nadu and Karnataka leveraged waivers to attract 10 GW+ projects under Solar Parks Scheme.

learn.title: Smart Grids & Advanced Metering: Digitizing Power
learn.intro: Smart grids use digital technology to enhance efficiency, reliability, and renewable integration. IEA emphasizes smart meters and automation as key to managing distributed energy resources, reducing outages, and enabling consumer participation in energy markets.
learn.c1_text: Smart meters provide real-time usage data and enable dynamic pricing. Like a car’s dashboard, they help consumers optimize energy use. IEA notes smart meters in India’s BSES service reduced AT&C losses by 18%, saving 2,000 MWh annually.
learn.c2_text: AI-driven analytics predict demand and integrate renewables. IEA reports smart grids can cut global carbon emissions by 1.5 Gt/year by 2050. Grid modernization in India’s Uttar Pradesh (2.5 million meters) improved outage response time by 40%.
learn.c3_text: MNRE’s Smart Grid Mission targets 200 million smart meters by 2025. BSES’s Rajasthan project achieved 99% reliability. IEA cites India’s ₹30,000 crore investment in grid modernization as critical for 500 GW renewable integration by 2030.
learn.stat2: AT&C loss reduction: 18% in BSES areas
learn.stat3: India’s smart meter target: 200 million by 2025
